messages.author: db3e727b0ff852e7
messages.subject: NA in numericInput?
parts:
Hi,
If a user deletes the value in a numericInput, the value that gets sent to the server is 0. Is it possible to change this behavior to send an NA instead?  Also, it would be good to be able to choose "NA" as the default value.

Thanks,
Brian

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: NA in numericInput?
parts:
I think you can already do that inside shinyServer. For example

output$foo <- reactive({
  if (input$bar == 0){
    input$bar = NA
  }
  ## rest of your code
})

Note that I am using syntax compatible with the latest development version of shiny on github.

messages.author: db3e727b0ff852e7
messages.subject: Re: NA in numericInput?
parts:
doesn't seem like it has to do with renderUI.

I updated the gist to include a renderUI slider and just a slider created in UI.R and they both seem to have the problem.

runGist(4981645)

On Feb 18, 2013, at 3:19 PM, Brian Bolt <brian...@gmail.com> wrote:

I can't seem to access to the second (high) value of the slider:

runGist(4981645)
https://gist.github.com/brianbolt/4981645


On Feb 18, 2013, at 3:10 PM, Brian Bolt <brian...@gmail.com> wrote:

I'm seeing an issue with slider inputs as well.  For some reason I can't access my renderUI slider like "input$yRange[[2]]".  I get a "subscript out of bounds" Not sure if it's related to this, or the recent api changes.  Trying to come up with a gist to demonstrate.  

On Feb 18, 2013, at 3:07 PM, Winston Chang <winsto...@gmail.com> wrote:

Just a heads up: it looks like the fix introduced a new bug, where sliderInputs send their updates immediately, without waiting for a slight pause first, so we'll have to address that now.

-Winston


On Mon, Feb 18, 2013 at 5:00 PM, Brian Bolt <brian...@gmail.com> wrote:
Great, thank you.


On Feb 18, 2013, at 2:02 PM, Winston Chang <winsto...@gmail.com> wrote:

The bug has been fixed in the master branch.

-Winston


On Mon, Feb 18, 2013 at 1:53 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
That's a bug, we'll get it fixed. Thanks!


On Sun, Feb 17, 2013 at 10:05 PM, Brian Bolt <brian...@gmail.com> wrote:
Yes, still not exactly.  I would prefer to override the default mechanism of numericInput as suggested above by Ramnath, but if it makes sense to add this to shiny as a default option, then I think it could benefit all.  Best to wait for the Shiny.


On Sunday, February 17, 2013 9:02:40 PM UTC-8, Vincent wrote:
How about using a selectInput with c(NA,1:20)? Not exactly what you are looking for but ...

On Sunday, February 17, 2013 7:36:47 PM UTC-8, Brian Bolt wrote:
I guess that is a possibility, but I would prefer if it was default behavior...if it makes sense to the Shiny team.

On Sunday, February 17, 2013 7:17:30 PM UTC-8, Ramnath Vaidyanathan wrote:
That makes sense. I believe the solution lies in modifying the numberInputBinding code here 

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/inst/www/shared/shiny.js#L1008-L1021



On Sunday, February 17, 2013 9:19:59 PM UTC-5, Brian Bolt wrote:
But there is a difference between a value not being set and the value being set to 0.  I would like to know when the field is empty or when it is filled with a 0

On Sunday, February 17, 2013 5:57:03 PM UTC-8, Ramnath Vaidyanathan wrote:
I think you can already do that inside shinyServer. For example

output$foo <- reactive({
  if (input$bar == 0){
    input$bar = NA
  }
  ## rest of your code
})

Note that I am using syntax compatible with the latest development version of shiny on github.

On Sunday, February 17, 2013 8:15:13 PM UTC-5, Brian Bolt wrote:
Hi,
If a user deletes the value in a numericInput, the value that gets sent to the server is 0. Is it possible to change this behavior to send an NA instead?  Also, it would be good to be able to choose "NA" as the default value.

Thanks,
Brian
